criminal-probe-after-deadly-jamaica-plai.title: Criminal Investigation Underway After Fatal Crash on the Arborway
criminal-probe-after-deadly-jamaica-plai.dek: Sunday, the Arborway, Jamaica Plain. A sedan crossed the median. A 48-year-old SUV driver was killed, according to reports.
body: Sunday. The Arborway in Jamaica Plain. One driver was killed and another critically injured in a crash, and the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office is conducting a criminal investigation, Boston.com reported, citing WHDH.

According to the reports, an 18-year-old was driving a white sedan. The driver lost control and jumped the concrete median. The sedan collided with a red SUV traveling in the opposite direction. The SUV's driver was 48 and was pronounced dead at the scene, Boston.com reported. Neither driver was named.

The 18-year-old was critically injured and taken to a local hospital, according to the report. Dash camera footage obtained by WHDH showed heavy damage to the driver's side of the SUV, Boston.com reported.

Sources told WHDH the sedan was going more than 50 mph, according to Boston.com. The speed limit on that stretch is 25 mph. The crash happened on a section of the parkway in Jamaica Plain, according to the report. The report did not give a time.

The district attorney's office did not respond to a request for comment on Monday, Boston.com reported. A nearby resident told WHDH he was concerned that drivers treat the parkways like racetracks. No charges had been reported. The investigation is ongoing.

driver-killed-in-jamaica-plain-crash-cri.title: Driver Killed in Jamaica Plain Crash; Criminal Investigation Underway
driver-killed-in-jamaica-plain-crash-cri.dek: Sunday, Jamaica Plain. One driver died and another was injured in a multi-car crash, a spokesperson for the Suffolk District Attorney's Office said.
body: Sunday, Jamaica Plain. A multi-car crash. One driver was killed and another was injured, according to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office, the Boston Globe reported.
A criminal investigation is being conducted, said James Borghesani, a spokesperson for the district attorney's office, according to the Globe. Police are also investigating.
Officials did not release the names of the drivers. They did not say what caused the crash. They did not give the condition of the injured driver, the Globe reported.
The Globe did not report where in Jamaica Plain the crash happened. It did not say how many vehicles were involved, beyond calling it a multi-car collision. No arrests or charges were mentioned.

No further information was immediately available from authorities, according to the Globe's report. It was published Sunday as a breaking news item in the paper's Crime and Courts section. The investigation remains ongoing. Officials had not said when more details would be released.

teen-turned-himself-in-after-fatal-hyde-.title: 18-Year-Old Charged With Murder in Hyde Park Gas Station Shooting
teen-turned-himself-in-after-fatal-hyde-.dek: The Boston man surrendered two days after a 20-year-old was fatally shot on Hyde Park Avenue, the Suffolk District Attorney's Office said.
body: Friday morning. An 18-year-old Boston man turned himself in to police. He pleaded not guilty to first-degree murder in the fatal shooting of a 20-year-old man at a Hyde Park gas station, according to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office, as reported by Boston.com.

Wednesday, Oct. 7, shortly after 5 p.m. A gas station at 1171 Hyde Park Ave. Police allege Christian Peebles shot the man inside, Boston.com reported. The man was taken to a local hospital. He was pronounced dead there. Authorities have released few details about the circumstances.

Peebles was arraigned in the West Roxbury Division of Boston Municipal Court on the murder charge and several firearms offenses, according to the report. He was ordered held without bail. Judge John Garland also revoked his bail in an earlier case. He is due back in court Nov. 9. He is presumed innocent.

His attorney, Jennifer O'Brien, said Peebles turned himself in once he learned police were looking for him. She said his parents brought him to the police station. She declined to comment further, citing the pending investigation.
The Boston Police Homicide Unit is investigating. Anyone with information can call 617-343-4470 or CrimeStoppers at 1-800-494-TIPS.

brighton-man-charged-in-triple-stabbing-.title: Brighton Man Arrested With Machete Also Charged in Triple Stabbing
brighton-man-charged-in-triple-stabbing-.dek: Boston police said detectives linked the 24-year-old to an Oct. 4 stabbing near Cambridge Street and Harvard Avenue. Three men were hurt.
body: A Brighton man was arrested Thursday, allegedly carrying a machete. He has also been charged in a triple stabbing in Brighton last weekend, according to Boston police, as reported by Boston.com.

Thursday, shortly before 5 p.m. Near Leo M. Birmingham Parkway. Officers responded to a report of a person swinging a large knife, police said. According to police, officers found Joshua Flores, 24, walking down Western Avenue with a machete. He dropped it when told to. Officers also found a folding knife in his pocket. He was first charged with carrying a dangerous weapon and disturbing the peace.

Police said detectives later developed probable cause to charge Flores in an earlier stabbing. Sunday, Oct. 4, about 1:30 a.m. Near Cambridge Street and Harvard Avenue. Officers there found three men with stab wounds. Boston EMS took them to hospitals. Their injuries were not considered life-threatening.

Flores is charged with three counts of armed assault with intent to murder, three counts of assault and battery with a dangerous weapon causing serious bodily injury and two counts of mayhem, Boston.com reported.
Judge Shelley Joseph ordered him held without bail pending a dangerousness hearing on Oct. 15. It was not immediately clear whether he had an attorney. He is presumed innocent.

arrest-in-hyde-park-avenue-homicide.title: Boston Man, 18, Charged With Murder in Hyde Park Avenue Shooting
arrest-in-hyde-park-avenue-homicide.dek: Boston police arrested an 18-year-old Friday in the fatal shooting of a 20-year-old man at 1171 Hyde Park Avenue two days earlier.
body: Friday. Boston police arrested an 18-year-old Boston man and charged him with murder in a fatal shooting on Hyde Park Avenue earlier in the week, according to a department release.
Police identified him as Christian Peebles, 18, of Boston. He was expected to be arraigned in West Roxbury District Court, the release said. Police did not describe how the arrest was made.

Wednesday, Oct. 7, about 5:09 p.m. 1171 Hyde Park Avenue. Officers answered a radio call for a person shot, police said. They found a man with a gunshot wound. He was taken to a local hospital and pronounced dead. Police said he was 20.
The department's Homicide Unit continues to review the facts and circumstances of the case, according to the release. Police did not say what led to the shooting.

Anyone with information is asked to call the Homicide Unit at 617-343-4470, police said. Tips can be shared anonymously by calling 1-800-494-TIPS or texting TIP to 27463. The department also listed the Boston Neighborhood Trauma Team's 24-hour support line, 617-431-0125. The murder charge is an allegation. Peebles is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

arrest-in-brighton-triple-stabbing.title: Brighton Man Arrested in Connection With Triple Stabbing
arrest-in-brighton-triple-stabbing.dek: A 24-year-old stopped with a machete on Western Avenue has been linked to the Oct. 4 stabbing of three men at Cambridge Street and Harvard Avenue, Boston police said.
body: Boston police have arrested a 24-year-old Brighton man. They say they have linked him to a stabbing that injured three men in Brighton last weekend, according to a department release.

Thursday, Oct. 8, about 4:54 p.m. Near Leo M. Birmingham Parkway and Waverly Street. Officers and detectives from District D-14 responded to a radio call about a person swinging a large knife, police said. Officers stopped the man in front of 444 Western Avenue. He dropped the knife when detectives ordered him to, according to the release. Police said they recovered a machete from the sidewalk. They recovered a folding knife from his pocket.

Police identified the man as Joshua Flores, 24, of Brighton. He was expected to be arraigned in Brighton District Court on charges of carrying a dangerous weapon and disturbing the peace, police said.

Detectives later developed probable cause linking Flores to an earlier stabbing, according to the release. Sunday, Oct. 4, about 1:30 a.m. Cambridge Street and Harvard Avenue. Officers responding to that call found three adult men with stab wounds. Boston EMS took them to local hospitals. Police described the injuries as not life-threatening.

In that incident, Flores faces three counts of armed assault with intent to murder, three counts of assault and battery with a dangerous weapon causing serious bodily injury and two counts of mayhem, police said. The charges are allegations. He is presumed innocent.

two-men-wanted-in-stabbing-of-nypd-detec.title: Two Men Wanted in Stabbing of NYPD Detective Arrested in Lynn
two-men-wanted-in-stabbing-of-nypd-detec.dek: A multi-agency team took the men into custody Tuesday night, U.S. Marshals said. They await extradition to New York.
body: Tuesday night, Lynn. Two men accused of stabbing an off-duty New York City police detective in the Bronx were arrested, according to the U.S. Marshals Service, as reported by Boston.com.

Friday, Oct. 2. According to the NYPD, the detective was stabbed several times and his chain was taken. The two men were last seen fleeing on a motorized bike, police said. The NYPD identified them as Dangelo Caraballo and Sneider Mejia.

The case went to the U.S. Marshals Service NY/NJ Regional Fugitive Task Force. Investigators learned the men had left the New York area together. They tracked them to Massachusetts, Boston.com reported. A multi-agency operation took both into custody in Lynn.

Dennis Matulewicz leads the Marshals Service in the District of Massachusetts. He called the stabbing an attack on every member of law enforcement. He credited cooperation among federal, state and local agencies.

Both men are being held by Massachusetts State Police while they await extradition to New York, according to the report. Both are presumed innocent. The specific charges were not reported. Neither was the detective's condition.

one-shot-overnight-near-central-square-i.title: One Person Shot Overnight Near Central Square in Cambridge
one-shot-overnight-near-central-square-i.dek: The person was in stable condition, Cambridge police said. Police said they do not believe there is a broader danger to the community.
body: Late Wednesday, near Central Square in Cambridge. One person was injured in a shooting, Cambridge police said, according to Boston.com.
Shortly before midnight. Near Columbia Terrace, off Columbia Street. Authorities received a report of a person shot, the Cambridge Police Department said in a Facebook post.
The person was taken to a local hospital. On Thursday, police said the victim was in stable condition. The injuries were not life-threatening. Police did not identify the person.

Police did not say whether a suspect had been identified. They did not say whether anyone had been arrested, Boston.com reported. The department said it does not believe there is any broader danger to the community.

The shooting remains under investigation. Anyone with information is asked to contact Cambridge detectives at 617-349-3300. Anonymous tips can be submitted by text or email following instructions on the department's website. Boston.com noted that one person was also injured in a separate shooting in North Cambridge on Tuesday.

man-shot-dead-in-hyde-park-gas-station.title: Police Seek Tips After Man Fatally Shot at Hyde Park Gas Station
man-shot-dead-in-hyde-park-gas-station.dek: Wednesday evening, a gas station on Hyde Park Avenue. A man was shot and killed. Boston police said they were still searching for a suspect.
body: Wednesday evening, a gas station on Hyde Park Avenue. A man was shot and killed. Boston police are asking the public for information, Boston.com reported.

About 5:09 p.m. Akiki Oil, 1171 Hyde Park Ave., police said, according to the report. Officers found a man suffering from a gunshot wound. Emergency crews took him to a local hospital. He was pronounced dead there, police said.

Police had not released the man's name. They did not say how the shooting happened, Boston.com reported. The Boston Police Homicide Unit is investigating. Police said they were still searching for a suspect. No arrests were reported at the time of publication.

Anyone with information is asked to call homicide detectives at 617-343-4470. Tips can be shared anonymously through the CrimeStoppers line at 1-800-494-TIPS or by texting TIP to 27463, according to police.

Police also noted that the Boston Neighborhood Trauma Team offers emotional support around the clock to people affected by violence. It can be reached at 617-431-0125, the report said. The investigation is ongoing. The suspect has not been named.

person-hospitalized-after-shooting-in-ca.title: Person Hospitalized After Late-Night Shooting in Cambridge
person-hospitalized-after-shooting-in-ca.dek: Just before midnight Wednesday, near Columbia Terrace. A person was shot. Cambridge police said they do not believe there is a wider threat to the public.
body: Just before midnight Wednesday. Columbia Terrace, Cambridge. A person was shot and taken to a hospital, police said, according to the Boston Globe.

Dispatchers were alerted shortly before midnight. Responders found the person who had been shot, the Globe reported. The person was taken to a local hospital. Police did not disclose the extent of the injuries.
Authorities did not release the person's name, age or any other identifying information, according to the newspaper.

Police said the shooting was under investigation. They said they did not believe there was a broader danger to the community, the Globe reported. No arrests were reported. Police did not release information about a suspect. They did not describe what led to the shooting.

The Globe's report was based on information from Cambridge police. It gave no location beyond Columbia Terrace. The investigation is continuing, police said. No additional information had been released about the person's condition.

man-shot-and-killed-in-hyde-park.title: Man Shot and Killed Inside Hyde Park Gas Station
man-shot-and-killed-in-hyde-park.dek: The shooting on Hyde Park Avenue did not appear to be random, Boston police said. No arrests had been made Wednesday evening.
body: Wednesday evening. A gas station and convenience store on Hyde Park Avenue. A man was shot and killed inside, Boston police said, according to the Boston Globe.

5:09 p.m. 1171 Hyde Park Ave. Police received a report of a person shot, the Globe reported. Officers found a man inside with a gunshot wound. He was taken to a local hospital. He was pronounced dead there.

Boston Police Superintendent Paul McLaughlin spoke at the scene. He said the man was a customer in the store. He said the man and the shooter may have known each other, according to the Globe. McLaughlin said the shooting did not appear to be random. Detectives were canvassing the area for video and witnesses, he said.

No arrests had been made. The death had not yet been ruled a homicide, police said. If it is, it would be Boston's 25th homicide this year, according to police. Sgt. Det. John Boyle described the case as an active investigation.
Anyone with information is asked to call homicide detectives at 617-343-4470 or to call 1-800-494-TIPS anonymously.

fourth-person-charged-in-deadly-june-sho.title: Fourth Person Charged in June Shooting in Mattapan That Killed One Man
fourth-person-charged-in-deadly-june-sho.dek: Suffolk prosecutors charged a 19-year-old Jamaica Plain man with first-degree murder in the June 27 shooting on Blue Hill Avenue. Four others were wounded.
body: A 19-year-old Jamaica Plain man has been charged with first-degree murder in a June shooting in Mattapan, the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office said. A 26-year-old Brockton man was killed. Four others were wounded.

Cerrone Wilcox Buford was charged in Suffolk Superior Court with murder, armed assault to murder, assault and battery with a dangerous weapon causing serious bodily injury and several firearm offenses, according to the DA's office. He was ordered held without bail. He is due back in court Nov. 3.

June 27. The backyard of 1460 Blue Hill Ave. Prosecutors said a fight began there and moved to the sidewalk out front. According to prosecutors, video and witnesses show Wilcox Buford taking a gun from a bag and aiming it at the man who was killed. At least seven shots were fired. Four people were wounded, the office said.

Three others have been charged, according to the release. Laquan Burris, 18, of Dorchester, and Javen Girault, 23, of Brockton, were ordered held on bail. They are due back Nov. 3. An arrest warrant has been issued for Mannice Mitchner, 19, of Boston. Prosecutors said Burris, Girault and Mitchner were among those wounded. All are presumed innocent.
District Attorney Kevin Hayden said the case shows the harm illegal guns cause. Mitchner has not been reported in custody.

detectives-find-knife-on-rooftop-arrest-.title: Revere Man Arrested in Roxbury Stabbing After Knife Found on Rooftop
detectives-find-knife-on-rooftop-arrest-.dek: Detectives used video and evidence at the scene to identify a suspect in the Sept. 29 attack near Warren Street, Boston police said.
body: Boston police have arrested a 31-year-old Revere man in a stabbing in Roxbury last month. Detectives recovered what appeared to be the knife from a nearby rooftop, according to a department release.

Tuesday, Sept. 29, about 7:12 p.m. Near 301 Warren St. Officers from District B-2 responded to a report of a person stabbed, police said. They spoke with witnesses. They followed evidence to a home on Kensington Park. There they found a 37-year-old man with a serious facial injury. He was taken to a local hospital. His condition was not reported.

According to preliminary information, the two men had argued inside a nearby business, police said. Investigators believe the suspect followed the man outside. They believe he attacked him with a knife near Warren and Dale streets.

Detectives collected evidence at the scene. They reviewed video from the business and nearby cameras to track the suspect's movements, according to the release. The next day, investigators found what appeared to be the knife on a rooftop. The Boston Fire Department helped recover it.

Police identified the suspect as Meshach Dowman. He is in custody. He will be arraigned in Roxbury District Court on charges of assault with intent to murder, mayhem and assault and battery by means of a dangerous weapon. He is presumed innocent. The injured man's condition has not been made public.

death-investigation-at-1171-hyde-park-av.title: Man Shot and Killed on Hyde Park Avenue; Homicide Unit Investigating
death-investigation-at-1171-hyde-park-av.dek: A man found with a gunshot wound at 1171 Hyde Park Avenue on Wednesday evening died at a hospital, Boston police said.
body: Wednesday evening, Hyde Park Avenue. A man was shot and died. The Boston Police Homicide Unit has opened an investigation, according to a department release.
Oct. 7, about 5:09 p.m. 1171 Hyde Park Avenue in Hyde Park. Officers from District E-18 responded to a radio call for a person shot, police said.
Officers found an adult man suffering from a gunshot wound, according to the release. He was taken to a local hospital. He was pronounced dead there. Police did not release his name or age.

The Homicide Unit is reviewing the facts and circumstances surrounding the incident, police said. The release did not mention a suspect. It did not mention an arrest or a possible motive. Police did not describe what led to the shooting.

Police asked anyone with information to call homicide detectives at 617-343-4470. Tips can be shared anonymously through the CrimeStoppers tip line at 1-800-494-TIPS or by texting the word TIP to 27463, according to the department. Police also directed anyone in need of support to the Boston Neighborhood Trauma Team. It offers free help at any hour at 617-431-0125. The investigation is ongoing.

missing-dorchester-teen-17-located.title: Missing 17-Year-Old From Dorchester Located, Boston Police Say
missing-dorchester-teen-17-located.dek: Boston police canceled a missing person alert for a Dorchester teenager last seen early Tuesday on Commonwealth Avenue.
body: A 17-year-old from Dorchester who had been reported missing has been located. The Boston Police Department said so in a notice canceling its missing person alert.

Tuesday, Oct. 6, about 4:30 a.m. The area of 540 Commonwealth Avenue. That is where the teen was last seen, police said in the original alert. The department had asked the public for help finding the teen.

The department later updated the alert. It said the teen had been found and the missing person alert was canceled. Police did not say where or when the teen was located. The notice gave no further details about the circumstances.

During the search, police had asked anyone with information about the teen's whereabouts to call 911 or District B-3 detectives at 617-343-4712. The department also directed people to share tips anonymously through its CrimeStoppers program, by phone at 1-800-494-TIPS, by texting the word TIP to 27463, or online, according to the release.
The teen is a minor. This report does not include the teen's name. The alert and its cancellation were issued by the department's Media Relations office.

one-hurt-in-shooting-near-cambridge-athl.title: One Person Injured in Shooting Near Russell Field in North Cambridge
one-hurt-in-shooting-near-cambridge-athl.dek: Tuesday afternoon, an athletic field off Rindge Avenue. One person was shot and hospitalized, police said.
body: Tuesday afternoon. Russell Field, North Cambridge. One person was injured in a shooting, according to Cambridge police, as reported by Boston.com.

About 3:20 p.m. Police said they received multiple calls reporting gunshots. The field sits off Rindge Avenue near the Alewife MBTA station. Sports teams from Cambridge Rindge and Latin School use it, Boston.com reported.

Emergency responders found one person with injuries related to the shooting. They took the victim to a local hospital, according to a Cambridge Police Department press release cited by Boston.com. Police said the victim's condition was not known. The victim was not identified.

A section of Rindge Avenue was closed off with police tape while investigators worked the scene, according to the report. Police said they did not believe there was any ongoing danger to the community.

Police did not say whether anyone had been arrested. They did not say whether a suspect had been identified. The investigation is ongoing. Anyone with information is asked to call Cambridge police detectives at 617-349-3300.

brockton-teen-struck-and-killed-crossing.title: Brockton Man, 18, Struck and Killed Crossing Route 44 in Raynham
brockton-teen-struck-and-killed-crossing.dek: Early Tuesday, New State Highway in Raynham. An 18-year-old Brockton man was hit by an SUV while crossing and died, officials said.
body: Early Tuesday morning. New State Highway, Raynham. An 18-year-old man from Brockton was struck and killed while crossing, according to Raynham police and fire officials, as reported by Boston.com.

About 6:15 a.m. Near 430 New State Highway. This section of Route 44 is lined with several businesses, including a gas station and a Dunkin', the report said. Officials said a Honda CR-V traveling west struck the man.

First responders treated him at the scene. They took him to Boston Medical Center-South in Brockton. He was later pronounced dead there, according to officials. Authorities had not publicly identified him.

The driver of the Honda, a 37-year-old Taunton man, remained at the scene, officials said. He and a passenger were taken by ambulance to Morton Hospital in Taunton to be evaluated, according to Boston.com.
Officials called the investigation preliminary. The report did not say whether any charges were being considered.

dorchester-man-20-charged-with-murder.title: Dorchester Man, 20, Charged With Murder After Whitfield Street Shooting
dorchester-man-20-charged-with-murder.dek: Police identified a 20-year-old Dorchester man as the suspect in the Sept. 30 shooting death of a man near 7 Whitfield Street, the Dorchester Post reported.
body: A 20-year-old Dorchester man has been charged with murder in a fatal shooting on Whitfield Street in Dorchester, the Dorchester Post reported.

Joseph Bailey was expected to be arraigned in Dorchester District Court, according to the Post. The report did not say whether the arraignment had taken place. It did not say whether bail had been set.

Wednesday, Sept. 30, about 5:39 p.m. Near 7 Whitfield Street. Officers were dispatched to a report of a person shot, according to the Post. They found an adult man with an apparent gunshot wound, the report said. He was taken to a local hospital. He was later pronounced dead. His name and age were not released.

After an investigation, detectives identified Bailey as the suspect, the Post reported. The circumstances of the shooting remain under investigation, according to the report. No other police or prosecutor statements were included.
The report did not list a next court date for Bailey. The murder charge is an allegation. Bailey is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

traffic-stop-in-dorchester-ends-in-gun-a.title: Traffic Stop on Washington Street in Dorchester Leads to Gun Arrest
traffic-stop-in-dorchester-ends-in-gun-a.dek: Boston police said they found a loaded handgun hidden in a car's radio casing after stopping a Quincy man driving on a suspended license.
body: Sunday night. Washington Street, Dorchester. Boston police arrested a Quincy man after a traffic stop. Officers said they found a loaded handgun concealed inside the car's radio casing, according to a department release.

Oct. 4, about 9:17 p.m. Near 156 Washington Street. Officers from District C-11 saw a man walk from a vehicle into a store, police said. A records check showed the vehicle operator's license was suspended, according to the release.

Officers said the man went back and forth between the store and the vehicle several times. He did not start the car. Officers briefly lost sight of him. Then they saw the vehicle drive away. They stopped it near 54 Washington Street, police said.

The driver got out. Officers noticed the gear shift box and radio appeared to have been tampered with, according to police. They saw the handle of a firearm inside the radio casing. They recovered a Glock 19 9mm handgun loaded with 11 rounds, the release said.

Police identified the driver as Johnny Williams Delacruz, 27, of Quincy. He was expected to be arraigned in Dorchester District Court, police said. The charges include carrying a loaded firearm without a license, possession of ammunition without an FID card, receiving stolen property and driving with a suspended license. He was also cited for motor vehicle violations. The charges are allegations. He is presumed innocent.

buyers-charged-in-cambridge-brothel-ring.title: Cases Against Men Charged in Cambridge Brothel Ring End With Fees, Classes
buyers-charged-in-cambridge-brothel-ring.dek: More than 30 men accused of paying for sex through a ring based near Alewife had their charges dropped under standard agreements. They were publicly identified, the Boston Globe reported.
body: The last criminal cases have concluded. More than 30 men were charged with paying for sex through a high-end brothel ring based near Alewife. Each accepted a standard agreement that led to dismissal of the charges, the Boston Globe reported in a story published on Boston.com.

The agreements were with Middlesex prosecutors. Each man paid a $2,000 fee to advocacy groups. Each attended a program aimed at reducing demand for paid sex. Each agreed to stay away from sex workers. The charges were dropped after nine months, according to the Globe. The men did not admit wrongdoing. They have no criminal records from the cases.

The ring operated out of luxury apartments in Cambridge and Watertown. Federal authorities described it as one of the most lucrative such networks on the East Coast, the Globe reported. Its three operators were Han Lee, James Lee and Junmyung Lee. They are not related. They pleaded guilty to federal charges after arrests in November 2023. Han Lee received the longest sentence, four years in prison.

Buying sex is a state misdemeanor. So the buyers were charged in state court, through hearings that are usually closed, according to the report. A clerk magistrate opened them to the public. The men lost a challenge at the Supreme Judicial Court. Authorities said they charged only men who had exchanged roughly 400 or more texts with the operators.

Unlike in earlier cases, the buyers were publicly identified, the Globe reported. Several lost their jobs. A former Cambridge city councilor did not seek reelection. One advocate who works with women leaving the sex trade praised authorities' handling of the case. Legal observers called the outcome normal under state law.

person-stabbed-in-downtown-crossing-life.title: Person Stabbed in Downtown Crossing Suffers Life-Threatening Injuries
person-stabbed-in-downtown-crossing-life.dek: Friday night, Tremont Street and Temple Place. A person was stabbed. Homicide detectives were called to investigate, Boston police said.
body: Friday night. Tremont Street and Temple Place, Downtown Crossing. A person was stabbed and taken to a hospital with life-threatening injuries, Boston police said, according to Boston.com.
About 10:55 p.m. Officers were called for a report of an assault in progress, police spokesperson Officer James Moccia told Boston.com. Officers found a person who had been stabbed, police said.

Emergency medical crews treated the victim at the scene. Then they took the person to a local hospital, according to the report. Police did not publicly identify the victim. They did not release the victim's age.
Homicide detectives were also called to investigate, Boston.com reported. Police did not describe what led up to the stabbing. They gave no information about a possible suspect.
As of Sunday morning, no arrests had been made, according to police. The investigation is ongoing. Police did not release any further details about the case.

woman-killed-when-vehicle-slams-into-fau.title: Woman Killed When Vehicle Strikes Building on Faulkner Hospital Campus
woman-killed-when-vehicle-slams-into-fau.dek: A woman sitting on a bench was killed when a vehicle crashed into a building at the Jamaica Plain hospital. Two people in the vehicle were hurt, the Boston Globe reported.
body: Thursday morning. The Brigham and Women's Faulkner Hospital campus in Jamaica Plain. A vehicle crashed into a building and a woman was killed, the Boston Globe reported. She had been sitting on a bench outside the building, according to the report.

The vehicle struck the Belkin House, a standalone building the hospital leases to a dialysis clinic. It came to rest between the parking garage entrance and the building's front steps, the Globe reported. A witness told the newspaper the crash happened at about 11 a.m. The woman was taken to the hospital's emergency department. She died there. Her name and age were not released.

Two people in the vehicle were injured and treated at the hospital, according to the Globe. The crash ruptured a gas line. More than 30 people were evacuated. Boston EMS paramedics who saw the crash called 911 and requested firefighters. Four paramedics were evaluated for exposure, the report said.

Boston Police Superintendent Paul McLaughlin said the preliminary investigation indicated the crash was not deliberate. He said police were not treating it as a crime, the Globe reported. A Mass General Brigham spokesperson offered condolences to the woman's family and to those injured. The spokesperson said staff could use an employee assistance program.

The Belkin House was closed as a precaution while crews checked gas lines, according to the report. Dialysis patients were directed to other locations. The cause of the crash remains under investigation.

man-accused-of-sexual-assaults-in-womens.title: Man Arrested in Alleged Sexual Assaults in Cambridge Gym Locker Room
man-accused-of-sexual-assaults-in-womens.dek: Thursday morning, a Porter Square gym. A 40-year-old man entered the women's locker room and assaulted people inside, Cambridge police said.
body: Thursday morning. A gym in Porter Square. Cambridge police arrested a man they say entered the women's locker room and sexually assaulted people inside, the Boston Globe reported.

The first report came in shortly after 9 a.m., according to police. The suspect was arrested at 9:22 a.m. Police did not name the gym. Planet Fitness confirmed to the Globe that the incident happened at its location. Police did not say how many people were assaulted. One woman was taken to a hospital for evaluation, the newspaper reported.
Police identified the man as Laquan Holland, 40, according to the Globe. Details of his arraignment were not immediately available.

Court records show Holland was charged in August in Cambridge District Court with failing to register as a sex offender, the Globe reported. That charge was dropped the same day. In 2006, he pleaded guilty to child rape and indecent assault charges, according to the newspaper.

Planet Fitness said it is committed to providing a safe environment, according to the Globe. It said it has canceled the man's membership and is cooperating with law enforcement. The investigation is ongoing. The new allegations have not been proven in court. Holland is presumed innocent.

police-release-photos-of-person-of-inter.title: Police Release Photos of Person Sought in Roxbury Stabbing
police-release-photos-of-person-of-inter.dek: Boston police are asking the public to help identify a person wanted in connection with a stabbing near Warren Street. The victim had a facial wound.
body: Tuesday evening, Roxbury. A stabbing. Boston police have released photos of a person they want to identify in connection with it, Boston.com reported.

Shortly after 7 p.m. The area of 201 Warren St. Officers were called there and found the victim in nearby Kensington Park, according to police. The victim had a serious cut to the face. The victim was taken to a local hospital with injuries police described as not life-threatening, the report said. The victim was not identified.

Officers searched the surrounding area. They did not locate the person responsible, police said. The department later released images of a person of interest and asked for the public's help, according to Boston.com.
Police did not describe what led to the stabbing. The report did not say whether the victim and the person being sought knew each other.

Anyone with information is asked to call District B-2 detectives at 617-343-4275. Tips can be shared anonymously by calling 1-800-494-TIPS or through the Boston Police Department website, police said. The investigation is ongoing. The person in the photos has not been named.

missing-14-year-old-mattapan-girl-found.title: Missing 14-Year-Old Mattapan Girl Found, Boston Police Say
missing-14-year-old-mattapan-girl-found.dek: A 14-year-old girl reported missing from Mattapan in mid-September has been located, Boston police announced.
body: Monday night, Boston police announced that a 14-year-old girl from Mattapan had been found, according to Boston.com. She had been missing since mid-September. Police released no other details about where or how she was located.
She was reported missing on Sept. 17, according to the report. Police said she was last seen at about 9 a.m. on Sept. 16. The area of Hillsboro Road in Mattapan.

During the search, police said she was known to spend time in the Grove Hall area, along Boylston Street and near Copley. They asked anyone who saw her to contact District B-3 detectives, Boston.com reported. The department had also invited the public to share anonymous tips by phone or through its website.
Police first asked the public for help in a missing person alert. Boston.com published it on Oct. 1. The news site later updated its report after police said she had been found.

During the search, police had asked anyone with information to call 911 or District B-3 detectives at 617-343-4712. After announcing she had been located, the department released no further information about her case, according to the report.

murder-charge-in-whitfield-street-killin.title: Boston Police Charge Suspect With Murder in Whitfield Street Homicide
murder-charge-in-whitfield-street-killin.dek: Detectives identified a 20-year-old Dorchester man as the suspect in the Sept. 30 fatal shooting near 7 Whitfield Street, police said.
body: Boston police have charged a 20-year-old Dorchester man with murder in the fatal shooting of a person near 7 Whitfield Street in Dorchester, according to a department release.

Wednesday, Sept. 30, about 5:39 p.m. Near 7 Whitfield Street. Officers from District B-2 responded to a radio call for a person shot, police said. They found a person with an apparent gunshot wound, according to the release. The victim was taken to a local hospital. The victim was later pronounced dead. Police did not release the victim's name or age.

Detectives identified Joseph Bailey, 20, of Dorchester, as the suspect, police said. He was expected to be arraigned in Dorchester District Court on a murder charge, according to the release. The release did not say when or how he was taken into custody.
The department's Homicide Unit continues to review the facts and circumstances of the incident, police said.

Police asked anyone with information to call the Homicide Unit at 617-343-4470. Tips, including photos and video, can be submitted anonymously by calling 1-800-494-TIPS, texting the word TIP to 27463 or using the department's online form, according to the release. The Boston Neighborhood Trauma Team offers free, confidential support at any hour at 617-431-0125. The charge is an allegation. Bailey is presumed innocent.

sexual-assaults-reported-in-cambridge-gy.title: Police Investigate Reported Sexual Assaults at Porter Square Planet Fitness
sexual-assaults-reported-in-cambridge-gy.dek: Thursday morning, the Massachusetts Avenue gym. A man entered the women's locker room and assaulted people inside, Cambridge police said, Boston.com reported.
body: Thursday morning. The Planet Fitness in Porter Square. Cambridge police responded to a report that a man had entered the women's locker room and sexually assaulted people inside, Boston.com reported.

Oct. 1, about 9:10 a.m. The gym at 1815 Massachusetts Ave., according to police. Officers located and apprehended a man police identified as Laquan Holland, Boston.com reported. The article did not list the charges he faces in Thursday's incident.
Police did not say how many people were assaulted, according to the report. One person was taken to a hospital for evaluation.

Court records show Holland pleaded guilty in 2006 to two counts of child rape and one count of indecent assault and battery on a child under 14, Boston.com reported. He was taken into custody on Aug. 25, 2026, on a charge of failing to register as a sex offender. That charge was later dismissed at the prosecution's request, according to the report.

Planet Fitness said it is committed to providing a safe environment for all members, Boston.com reported. It said the franchise group canceled the man's membership. It said it is cooperating with law enforcement. Cambridge police said the investigation is ongoing. They had no further details as of Thursday evening. The new allegations have not been proven. Holland is presumed innocent.

teele-square-fire-displaces-more-than-40.title: Somerville Activates Displacement Fund After Teele Square Fire
teele-square-fire-displaces-more-than-40.dek: A five-alarm fire at a three-story building on Broadway displaced 43 residents from 32 homes. The city opened its emergency fund, Boston.com reported.
body: Wednesday. A three-story apartment building spanning 1137 to 1147 Broadway in Somerville's Teele Square. A five-alarm fire displaced 43 people, according to the Somerville Fire Department, as reported by Boston.com.

The fire began just before 5 p.m. on Sept. 30, the report said. Smoke first appeared on the third floor. Fire conditions were heavy above the ceiling, according to the fire department. Crews sent five aerial ladders to the roof. They cut holes in it to release smoke. Firefighting operations were scaled back at about 10 p.m., Boston.com reported.

All occupants got out safely. Thirty-two homes were affected, according to the report. Several firefighters suffered minor injuries. They were not taken to the hospital, the fire department said. The third floor and roof sustained fire, smoke and water damage. The lower floors had extensive water damage. A laundromat, a smoke shop and a seafood restaurant on the ground floor were reported closed.

Departments from Arlington, Boston, Brookline, Belmont, Cambridge, Chelsea, Everett, Malden, Medford, Revere and Watertown assisted, according to Boston.com. Stoneham covered Somerville's central fire station. Mayor Jake Wilson praised the responders and neighboring departments for preventing a worse outcome.
The city has activated its emergency displacement fund for affected residents, Boston.com reported. The cause of the fire has not been determined.

five-alarm-fire-in-somervilles-teele-squ.title: Five-Alarm Fire in Somerville's Teele Square Displaces 43 Residents
five-alarm-fire-in-somervilles-teele-squ.dek: A fire at a mixed-use building on Broadway displaced 43 residents from 32 units. Two firefighters went to the hospital with minor injuries, the Boston Globe reported.
body: Wednesday. A mixed-use building in Somerville's Teele Square. A five-alarm fire spread through it and displaced 43 residents from 32 apartments, the Boston Globe reported.

The fire broke out at 1135 Broadway, at the corner of Curtis Street, according to the Globe. It is a brick building with apartments upstairs and businesses on the ground floor, including a laundromat and two restaurants. Medford firefighters returning from another call spotted smoke between the third floor and the roof. They reported it, the newspaper said.

The fire peaked shortly before 5 p.m., according to the report. It was under control by about 6 p.m. It was largely out by 7 p.m. Crews from Revere, Lexington, Everett, Arlington, Chelsea, Medford and Cambridge assisted. All residents got out safely. Two firefighters were treated at a hospital for minor injuries, the Globe reported.

Fire officials said Thursday the fire was confined to third-floor units, according to the newspaper. It spread along the ceilings and beneath the roof across 1137 to 1147 Broadway. The third floor and roof sustained heavy fire, smoke and water damage. The lower floors had extensive water damage. Somerville Fire Chief Charles Breen said many of the ground-floor businesses will likely be closed.

The American Red Cross is helping displaced residents find temporary housing, the Globe reported. It is working with the city's Board of Health to identify those affected. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

man-shot-in-dorchester-homicide-detectiv.title: Man Shot in Dorchester Apartment; Homicide Detectives Respond
man-shot-in-dorchester-homicide-detectiv.dek: Wednesday evening, an apartment on Whitfield Street. A man was shot and taken to a hospital with life-threatening injuries, Boston police said.
body: Wednesday evening. An apartment on Whitfield Street in Dorchester. A man was shot inside and taken to a hospital with life-threatening injuries, officials said, according to the Boston Globe.

About 5:40 p.m. 7 Whitfield St. Boston police said officers responded to a report of a person shot, the Globe reported. First responders found a man suffering from a gunshot wound, according to police.
The man was taken to a hospital, officials said. His condition was not immediately known. Authorities did not release his name or age, the newspaper reported.

Investigators from the Boston Police Department's homicide unit went to the scene, according to the Globe. Police said the shooting remained under investigation. The report had no information about a suspect. No arrests had been announced.

The Globe described its story as breaking news. It said the story would be updated as more information became available. The report did not say what led to the shooting. It did not describe any possible suspect.

detectives-no-longer-seeking-public-help.title: Boston Police Cancel Public Appeal in Roxbury Stabbing Investigation
detectives-no-longer-seeking-public-help.dek: Detectives said they no longer need the public's help identifying a person in a Tuesday evening stabbing near Warren Street. The investigation continues.
body: Boston police have canceled a community alert in a Roxbury stabbing. The alert asked the public to help identify a person. Detectives no longer need that assistance, according to an updated department release.

Tuesday, Sept. 29, about 7:12 p.m. Near 301 Warren Street. Officers from District B-2 responded to a call for a person stabbed, police said. Officers later found the victim in Kensington Park with a serious cut to the face, according to the release.

The victim was taken to a local hospital with injuries police described as not life-threatening, the release said. Officers searched the area for the person responsible. They did not find anyone at the time, according to police.

The department had released three images of an individual it wanted to identify. The updated notice is marked as a cancellation. It states that detectives are no longer seeking the public's help with the identification. It does not say whether anyone has been identified. It does not say whether anyone has been arrested.

District B-2 detectives are continuing to investigate, police said. Anyone with information can call detectives at 617-343-4275 or share tips anonymously by calling 1-800-494-TIPS, by texting the word TIP to 27463, or through the department's online CrimeStoppers page, according to the release.

police-say-accused-kidnapper-threatened-.title: Roxbury Man Charged Federally in Alleged Rhode Island Kidnapping
police-say-accused-kidnapper-threatened-.dek: Federal prosecutors say a 31-year-old Roxbury man forced a person from their Rhode Island home into a car and drove into Massachusetts. The car crashed on I-93.
body: A 31-year-old Roxbury man has been charged in federal court with kidnapping a person from their home in Rhode Island and driving them into Massachusetts, according to Boston.com, which cited a release from the U.S. Attorney's Office in Massachusetts.
Dominic Hampton-Boyd is charged with kidnapping and with being a felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition, the report said.

Aug. 12. A home in Rhode Island. Prosecutors allege Hampton-Boyd entered the victim's home and struck the victim with a pistol. They allege he forced the victim into a car and asked whether they wanted to "die here or in Boston." According to prosecutors, he then drove into Massachusetts. The victim tried several times to get out of the car.

The victim called 911, prosecutors said. Police tried to pull the car over. Hampton-Boyd allegedly sped up, struck several vehicles on Interstate 93 and crashed. He ran. He was caught, according to the report. Police said they recovered a privately made, Glock-style pistol loaded with 9mm ammunition from the car. Prosecutors said prior state convictions, including armed robbery, bar him from having guns or ammunition. The victim was not identified.

Hampton-Boyd is being held in state custody, Boston.com reported. He will appear in federal court in Boston at a later date. No date was given. The kidnapping charge carries a possible sentence of up to life in prison. The charges are allegations. He is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

man-killed-in-shooting-on-walter-street-.title: Milton Man Killed in Shooting Inside Hyde Park Business
man-killed-in-shooting-on-walter-street-.dek: Saturday afternoon, near 54 Walter Street. A 37-year-old Milton man was fatally shot, Boston police said. The homicide unit is investigating.
body: Saturday afternoon. A business on Walter Street in Hyde Park. A 37-year-old man from Milton was shot and killed inside, according to the Boston Police Department.

Sept. 26, about 1:09 p.m. Near 54 Walter Street. Officers from District E-18 responded to a radio call for a person shot inside a business, police said in a release. Officers found a man with multiple gunshot wounds, according to the department.
Boston EMS pronounced the man dead at the scene, police said.
The Boston Police Homicide Unit is reviewing the facts and circumstances of the shooting, according to the release. Police announced no arrests. They released no information about a suspect.

Police asked anyone with information to contact homicide detectives at 617-343-4470. Tips can be shared anonymously by calling 1-800-494-TIPS or by texting the word TIP to 27463, according to the department. The department also noted that the Boston Neighborhood Trauma Team offers free emotional support around the clock to residents affected by violence, at 617-431-0125.
The investigation remains open, police said. The man has not been named.

detectives-seek-suspects-in-dorchester-a.title: Detectives Seek Two Men in Armed Robbery of Blue Hill Avenue Store
detectives-seek-suspects-in-dorchester-a.dek: Thursday morning, a Dorchester store. Two men robbed it at gunpoint, Boston police say. Police released images and asked for help identifying them.
body: Thursday morning. A store on Blue Hill Avenue in Dorchester. An armed robbery. Boston police are asking the public to help identify two men, according to a department community alert.
Sept. 24, about 11:15 a.m. 322 Blue Hill Avenue. Officers from District B-2 responded to a radio call for an armed robbery, police said.

Police described the victim's account. One man pointed a firearm at the victim and demanded money. The second man went behind the counter. The two took all of the cash from the store's register and its lottery register, police said. They fled along Lawrence Street toward Normandy Street, according to the alert. The release did not report any injuries.
The department released images of the two men. District B-2 detectives are actively investigating. No arrests had been announced, according to the alert. The men have not been identified.

Anyone with information is asked to call detectives at 617-343-5628, the number listed in the release. Tips can also be shared anonymously through CrimeStoppers by calling 1-800-494-TIPS, by texting the word TIP to 27463, or through the department's online form, police said.

man-set-off-explosive-device-during-stan.title: Man Set Off Explosive Device During Police Confrontation in Charlestown
man-set-off-explosive-device-during-stan.dek: Early Monday, Mishawum and Main streets. A man detonated a device worn around his neck and was seriously injured before being taken into custody, Boston police said.
body: Early Monday, Charlestown. A man detonated an explosive device during a confrontation with Boston police officers. He was seriously injured, according to police, as reported by Boston.com. He has been charged with possessing and discharging explosives, authorities said.

About 1 a.m. The area of Mishawum and Main streets. Police said officers were called after the man reported that he did not feel safe there. Officers found him holding a device with wires running around his neck. He told them it was explosive, according to a police incident report cited by Boston.com.

Members of the department's special operations team tried to disarm him using flash-bang devices and other less-lethal munitions, police said. According to the report, the man was struck several times. He still set off the device. It exploded near his chest. Officers then took him into custody with the help of a K-9 unit.

The man was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital with serious injuries, according to Boston.com. Police said he told officers he did not intend to harm them. During treatment, he told officers there were more explosive materials in his vehicle. The bomb unit searched the vehicle and towed it as evidence, police said.
Police did not release the man's name or age. The charges are allegations. He is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

upper-east-side-capital-one-brick-hate-c.title: Hate Crimes Task Force Investigates Brick Attack on Upper East Side Bank
upper-east-side-capital-one-brick-hate-c.dek: Oct. 19, morning, East 86th Street. A brick went through the front window of a Capital One bank, and graffiti referenced Palestine Action and the Israeli defense company Elbit, police said.
body: Monday, Oct. 19, about 7:50 a.m. 247 East 86th Street, the Upper East Side. Someone threw a brick through the front window of the Capital One bank there, according to ABC7 New York.
Capital One reported damage to multiple glass panels. The front of the branch had been tagged with red spray paint, the station reported.
## The Graffiti

Authorities said the graffiti read "Pal Action" and "Drop Elbit." Palestine Action is an activist movement that protests defense companies linked to Israel, including the Israeli weapons maker Elbit Systems. Activists have previously targeted Capital One over its lending to Elbit, ABC7 reported.

The NYPD's Hate Crimes Task Force took over the investigation. Police had not publicly specified a motive as of the station's report. No one had been arrested. No one had been identified as a suspect. Investigators were canvassing the neighborhood for surveillance video.
No one was hurt.
## Officials and Neighbors
City Council Speaker Julie Menin, who represents the Upper East Side, posted about the attack on social media, as did other local officials, according to ABC7.

Andrew Kavesh is a neighbor and a customer of the bank. He told the station the attack was frightening. He said that if it turns out to be a hate crime, particularly one aimed at Jewish people, it would feel deeply personal to him.
> "It's scary." — Andrew Kavesh, Upper East Side resident
## The Count

The NYPD reports a rise in bias crime even as overall crime falls. Through the first nine months of 2026, confirmed hate crimes rose 12.9% citywide. More than half were anti-Jewish, according to department figures reported by ABC7 on Oct. 7. Over the same period, major crime fell 6.6%.

Whether the Capital One attack is classified as a hate crime will depend on what investigators determine about who threw the brick and why. As of Monday, investigators had not said whether they believed the attack was connected to earlier protests against the bank.
Anyone with information is asked to call NYPD Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS.

fatal-shooting-seventh-avenue-53rd-stree.title: Man, 26, Shot Dead on Midtown E Train Platform; Gunman Fled on the 7
fatal-shooting-seventh-avenue-53rd-stree.dek: Oct. 17, the Seventh Avenue-53rd Street station. A 26-year-old Bronx man was shot dead after an argument. Two days later, police were still looking for the gunman.
body: Saturday, Oct. 17, shortly before 12:30 p.m. The uptown E train platform at the Seventh Avenue-53rd Street station. An argument ended there. A 26-year-old man from the Bronx was left with a gunshot wound to the chest, according to ABC7 New York.

Police said the gunman walked up to the victim, pulled a pistol and fired. Investigators told the station the dispute spilled onto a train and then back onto the platform. The victim was rushed to Bellevue Hospital in critical condition. He later died.
## On the Platform

Riders who were on the platform described terror. A woman performed CPR on the wounded man before emergency crews arrived, ABC7 reported. One witness told the station people had huddled together when the gunman fired again. Then riders ran for the stairs.
According to police, the shooter boarded a northbound 7 train and was gone. Investigators were still working to determine whether shots were fired on the platform, on the train, or both.
## 'Not a Random Act'

Police described the killing as targeted. They said it was not a random act. They said they would find the person responsible, ABC7 reported. Sources told the station the two men had been arguing on the platform before the shooting. What started the dispute has not been made public.
The NYPD released surveillance images of the suspect. He was described as wearing red clothing, a black vest and a face mask. As of Monday, Oct. 19, no arrest had been announced.
## The Victim

Neighbors told ABC7 the victim worked as a security guard. He was a twin. His brother is a Marine stationed in Texas. Relatives and neighbors gathered over the weekend to remember him. Detectives canvassed for video along the 7 line.
## Riders
Commuters told amNY the killing resurfaced their anxiety about daily conditions underground. They described open drug use, fights, and people in visible mental health crisis on trains and platforms.

NYPD data cited by amNY show subway crime was up 0.9% as of Oct. 1. Most of that came from an 11% rise in felony assaults. Over the same stretch, shootings and murders citywide fell to record lows through September.
Police ask anyone with information to call the NYPD Crime Stoppers hotline at 1-800-577-TIPS. The gunman has not been named.

arverne-teen-charged-murder-14-year-old-.title: Rockaway Teen Charged With Murder of 14-Year-Old Over a Scooter
arverne-teen-charged-murder-14-year-old-.dek: A 17-year-old from Far Rockaway was held without bail on Oct. 14. He is charged with murder in the Sept. 21 shooting death of a 14-year-old boy at the Ocean Bay Apartments in Arverne.
body: Monday, Sept. 21, about 3:33 p.m. The courtyard of the Ocean Bay Apartments in Arverne. A 14-year-old boy rode in on a push scooter with three others. Minutes later he was on the ground with a bullet in his back, according to Queens prosecutors as reported by QNS.

Tuesday, Oct. 13, about 11:30 a.m. Three weeks after the killing. A 17-year-old from Far Rockaway walked into the 101st Precinct station house and surrendered to detectives, QNS reported, citing a law enforcement source. He was booked on murder and weapons charges. He is not being named here because he is a minor.
## What Prosecutors Allege

The criminal complaint was described by QNS. According to it, the teen approached the 14-year-old beside a residential building at 51-24 Beach Channel Drive and fired twice. One round struck the boy in the lower back and traveled to his heart.

Police said the encounter began as an attempted robbery, QNS reported. They said the suspect pulled a handgun during a struggle. After the boy fell, prosecutors allege, the teen took the scooter and fled east on Norton Avenue. He changed clothes in a public bathroom. Investigators later recovered the clothing from a trash bin there, according to the complaint.
EMS rushed the boy to Cohen Children's Medical Center in Glen Oaks. He underwent emergency surgery. He was pronounced dead at the hospital.
> "A targeted, execution-style killing." — Queens District Attorney Melinda Katz
Katz said that, as alleged, the victim was shot through his heart, QNS reported.
## In Court

Wednesday, Oct. 14. Queens Supreme Court. The 17-year-old was arraigned on charges of second-degree murder and two counts of second-degree criminal possession of a weapon. Justice Seth Steed ordered him held without bail. He set a return date of Oct. 19, according to QNS.
If convicted, he faces up to 25 years to life in prison. The charges are accusations. He is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.
## Where It Happened

The Ocean Bay Apartments are a sprawling public housing complex along Beach Channel Drive. They sit at the far end of the Rockaway peninsula, one of the city's most isolated corners. The A train and the ferry are the main links to the rest of the city.

The NYPD reports historically low gun violence. Through September, the department counted 203 murders citywide, the fewest on record for the first nine months of a year, ABC7 New York reported. One of them was a 14-year-old in Arverne.

off-duty-detective-stabbed-norwood-robbe.title: Off-Duty Detective Stabbed Over Gold Chain Chased Attackers Five Blocks
off-duty-detective-stabbed-norwood-robbe.dek: NYPD Detective Jose Mercedes was stabbed repeatedly during an attempted robbery in Norwood on Oct. 2. He spoke publicly for the first time on Oct. 13. Two men arrested in Massachusetts faced charges in the Bronx.
body: Oct. 2. Near East 206th Street and Rochambeau Avenue in Norwood, the Bronx's 52nd Precinct. Detective Jose Mercedes was on vacation. He was standing at the trunk of his car. Two men on an e-bike came up behind him, according to ABC7 New York and amNY.
They wanted the gold chain around his neck, a gift from his mother, ABC7 reported. Mercedes, 33, fought back. He told them, in English and in Spanish, that he was a police officer.
> "They didn't care." — NYPD Detective Jose Mercedes
## The Wounds

Mercedes was stabbed seven times, according to amNY. ABC7 reported he was stabbed 10 times. He lost a significant amount of blood, ABC7 reported. According to his union, he did not go down. Detectives' Endowment Association President Scott Munro said Mercedes chased the attackers for five blocks while bleeding.
He was taken to Jacobi Hospital and released on Oct. 4, amNY reported. He has not returned to work. He is concentrating on regaining mobility in his left hand, according to ABC7.
## First Words in Public

Tuesday, Oct. 13. DEA headquarters in Lower Manhattan. Mercedes stood before cameras, surrounded by colleagues who came to welcome him back, amNY reported. He told reporters he was happy to be alive, ABC7 reported. He said he had never expected to be attacked while simply trying to enjoy his time off. He thanked fellow officers and federal partners for tracking down the suspects.
## The Arrests in Lynn

Five days after the stabbing, the two men police accuse were arrested in Lynn, Massachusetts. The New York–New Jersey Regional Fugitive Task Force and the U.S. Marshals made the arrests, according to Munro, as reported by amNY. Munro identified them as D'Angelo Rafael Jean Caraballo and Sneider Mejia Bautista. He said they face charges including attempted murder.

ABC7 described the two as undocumented Dominican nationals with lengthy criminal histories. It reported they had been extradited to New York and were expected to be arraigned in the Bronx on Wednesday, Oct. 14. The men have not been convicted. The allegations against them have not been tested in court.

Munro's union has been feuding with the Civilian Complaint Review Board and City Hall over discipline. He used the moment to call for long prison terms. A photo caption in amNY said he urged 25 years to life for the suspects.

There has been a run of violence against officers in the Bronx. Saturday, Oct. 17, evening. Near Garrison Avenue and Whittier Street in Hunts Point. A uniformed officer responding to a loud music call was struck by a white Honda SUV, ABC7 reported. The driver fled. The officer suffered a leg injury. No arrest had been announced.

selma-blair-arrested-jfk-delta-flight.title: Selma Blair Taken Into Custody at JFK After Flight Attendants Report Attack
selma-blair-arrested-jfk-delta-flight.dek: Oct. 11, JFK Airport. Police were called about a physically abusive passenger on Delta Flight 938 from Los Angeles. Actress Selma Blair was taken into custody. Her representative blamed a medical emergency.
body: Sunday, Oct. 11, about 11 p.m. John F. Kennedy International Airport. Delta Air Lines Flight 938 from Los Angeles was parked at the gate. Port Authority police were called to deal with a physically abusive passenger, according to amNY.
The passenger was the actress Selma Blair, 54. She was taken into custody immediately and brought to a nearby hospital for evaluation, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey said.
## What Allegedly Happened

Accounts of the flight remain secondhand. Multiple reports cited by amNY said Blair bit a member of the crew and tried to open a door of the aircraft. Variety, citing TMZ, reported that she tried to open the door while the plane was in the air. It reported she punched one flight attendant and bit another.
Two flight attendants reported injuries. One was taken to a hospital for further evaluation, amNY reported.

The Port Authority said the FBI is investigating. That is standard when alleged crimes occur aboard an aircraft in flight. As of amNY's report on Oct. 12, it was not clear what charges, if any, Blair would face. It was not clear whether she had appeared in court. The allegations have not been proven.
## 'A Medical Emergency'
A representative for Blair told Variety that a medical emergency led to the incident. The representative said she received immediate medical attention after landing and was in stable condition.

Blair is known for films including Cruel Intentions and Legally Blonde. She has spoken publicly for years about living with multiple sclerosis. Her representative did not specify the nature of the emergency on the flight, according to the reports.
## The Airline
A Delta spokesperson told amNY the incident had no operational impact. The spokesperson said the flight landed ahead of schedule.
> "Delta has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior." — Delta spokesperson
The spokesperson added that the safety of customers and crew always comes first.

Assaults on flight crews have become a recurring concern for the airline industry. Federal law treats interference with flight crew members as a serious offense. Whether the case moves forward depends on what investigators conclude about the events in the cabin and the medical circumstances Blair's camp has described. No charges have been announced.

allerton-balcony-mother-killed-infant-su.title: Bronx Mother Killed, Infant Daughter Survives After Police Say Both Were Pushed From Balcony
allerton-balcony-mother-killed-infant-su.dek: Oct. 6, Allerton. A 23-year-old woman died and her 8-month-old daughter was critically injured after police say both were pushed from a 15th-floor balcony. The NYPD is seeking the child's father.
body: Tuesday, Oct. 6, around 3:30 a.m. The Allerville Arms, an apartment tower on Olinville Avenue in the Allerton section of the Bronx. Officers found a 23-year-old woman and her 8-month-old daughter on the ground outside, according to ABC7 New York.
Police say both had been pushed from a 15th-floor balcony.
## To Jacobi
Officers did not wait for an ambulance. They put the baby in a patrol car and took her to Jacobi Hospital, ABC7 reported. The mother was also taken to the hospital. She was pronounced dead there.

The infant survived the fall. By Wednesday, Oct. 7, she was in critical but stable condition. Police said they believed she would live. Investigators told the station they believe the mother fell in a way that cushioned the impact for her daughter.
## The Search

The NYPD said the woman's death is being investigated as a homicide. Detectives are seeking a 31-year-old man believed to be her ex-boyfriend and the child's father. They released his photo, ABC7 reported. Authorities said surveillance video captured him leaving the building. As of the station's Oct. 8 update, no arrest had been announced. He has not been charged with a crime.
Investigators are still working to determine what happened inside the apartment in the hours before dawn.
## Earlier Calls

Sources told Eyewitness News there was a documented history of domestic violence at the apartment. They said police had responded there twice in January. A neighbor told the station that earlier this year they saw a man trying to kick in the apartment door.

Stephanie McGraw is founder and chief executive of the Harlem domestic violence organization WARM. She told ABC7 the woman was one of roughly seven women killed in New York City over the past two months.

The NYPD calls this a historic year for public safety. Murders through September were at their lowest level on record. Domestic violence often happens behind closed doors. Earlier calls for help can leave a record that investigators read only afterward.
Anyone with information is asked to contact NYPD Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS. People experiencing domestic violence in New York City can reach the city's 24-hour hotline at 1-800-621-HOPE.

nypd-record-low-shootings-murders-septem.title: NYC Shootings and Murders Hit Record Lows Through September
nypd-record-low-shootings-murders-septem.dek: The city recorded 489 shooting incidents and 203 murders in the first nine months of 2026, the NYPD said Oct. 6. Both are the lowest totals for that period in its records.
body: Tuesday, Oct. 6. The NYPD released its crime figures for the first nine months of the year, according to ABC7 New York. For a city long defined by its violence numbers, they were the lowest on record.

January through September. 489 shooting incidents. 594 shooting victims. 203 murders. Each figure is the lowest for the first nine months of any year in the department's records. Compared with the same stretch of 2021, 846 fewer people were shot.
> "The fewest shooting incidents, shooting victims, and murders." — NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch
Tisch said the totals were the lowest for the first nine months of any year in recorded history, ABC7 reported.
## Every Borough Down

Major crime fell 6.6% citywide, from 92,057 reported incidents to 86,023. It dropped in all five boroughs. The Bronx, long the center of the city's gun violence, posted the steepest decline, 11.9%, according to the NYPD figures.
The third quarter alone set records. July through September: 167 shooting incidents, 213 shooting victims and 73 murders, each the lowest on record for that quarter. Major crime fell 9.4%.

Robbery was down 12.2%. Burglary, 13.7%. Grand larceny, 5.8%. Auto theft, 12.4%. In public housing, murders, shootings, shooting victims and robberies all reached record lows for the first nine months. Major crime there fell 6.5%, ABC7 reported.
## Where It Rose

Not every line went down. Felony assaults rose 0.2%. Reported rapes rose 3.7%. Police said that partly reflects recent reports of incidents from previous years. Confirmed hate crimes rose 12.9%. More than half were anti-Jewish, according to the department.

Transit crime was roughly flat, up 0.9%. The NYPD said 2026 ranks among the safest years in the subway in 15 years, excluding the pandemic-era ridership collapse. Tisch vowed to go after the people driving violence underground.
## Credit and Caveats

Police credited gun seizures, gang takedowns and data-driven deployments. Mayor Zohran Mamdani credited both officers and violence-prevention programs. He noted that major crime fell in every borough, ABC7 reported.

The figures arrive at a politically delicate moment for the mayor. He is resisting pressure from parts of his own coalition to replace Tisch. Days after the release, on Oct. 17, a man was shot dead on a Midtown E train platform. Year-to-date numbers do not account for a single shooting, or for how riders feel after one.

manhunt-continues-for-gunman-in-deadly-m.title: Police Search for Gunman After Fatal Shooting on Midtown Subway Platform
manhunt-continues-for-gunman-in-deadly-m.dek: Saturday, an E train platform at the Seventh Avenue station. A 26-year-old Bronx man was shot and killed. Police have released images of a man they are seeking.
body: Saturday afternoon. A Midtown subway platform. A 26-year-old man from the Bronx was fatally shot. Police are still looking for the gunman, NY1 reported.

About 12:20 p.m. The northbound E train platform at the Seventh Avenue station near West 53rd Street. The man was shot once in the chest, according to police. He was taken to Bellevue Hospital. He was pronounced dead there. Investigators said the shooting followed an argument between two men.

Police released surveillance images of a man wanted in the killing. He was last seen wearing a red tracksuit, a black vest and a black face mask, police said. He was carrying a backpack. No arrest had been announced as of Sunday evening, according to NY1.

MTA Chief Security Officer Michael Kemper said the agency is working with police. He said it is reviewing camera footage from the platform and train cars. He said guns have no place in the transit system. An MTA spokesperson declined to comment Sunday. The NYPD did not respond to NY1's request for comment on a possible face-covering ban.

On Sunday, the rider advocacy group Passengers United gathered at the station. It called for a ban on face masks in the transit system. Its president, Charlton D'Souza, argued that masks make it harder for police to identify suspects. Riders who spoke to NY1 said the killing left them feeling unsafe.
Anyone with information is asked to call NYPD Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS. The gunman has not been identified.

teenager-slashed-in-ridgewood-morning-as.title: Teenager Slashed in Ridgewood Morning Assault; Suspect at Large
teenager-slashed-in-ridgewood-morning-as.dek: Monday morning, Myrtle and Forest avenues. A 17-year-old was cut on the hand. Police are searching for a young suspect who fled on foot.
body: Monday morning. Near Myrtle and Forest avenues in Ridgewood, Queens. A 17-year-old boy was slashed. Police are searching for the suspect, amNY reported.
Oct. 19, about 7:50 a.m., according to amNY. Officers from the 104th Precinct found the teen with a cut to his right hand. EMS took him to Bellevue Hospital. He was listed in stable condition.
Police do not yet know what led to the attack, amNY reported. Police sources said, based on a preliminary investigation, that the suspect may have known the victim.

Police described the suspect as a male aged 17 to 18. He was last seen wearing a black hooded sweatshirt with a spider logo and carrying a Nike backpack. He fled south on Forest Avenue. He remains at large, according to amNY.
The 104th Precinct has recorded 263 assaults this year through Oct. 11, up 14.3% from the same point in 2025, amNY reported. Anyone with information can call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

upper-east-side-bank-vandalized-nypd-pro.title: Upper East Side Bank Vandalized; NYPD Probes Possible Hate Crime
upper-east-side-bank-vandalized-nypd-pro.dek: Monday morning, East 86th Street. Windows at a Capital One branch were smashed. Pro-Palestinian messages were painted on its doors.
body: Monday morning. A Capital One branch at 249 East 86th Street on the Upper East Side. Front windows were smashed. Messages were painted on the doors. The NYPD Hate Crimes Task Force is investigating, amNY reported.

Oct. 19, about 7:40 a.m. Officers from the 19th Precinct responded to a report. They found several windows broken, apparently with bricks, according to amNY. Other windows and the front doors were marked with red stenciled letters reading "PAL ACTION" and "DROP ELBIT."

ABC7 reported that the first phrase may refer to Palestine Action, a U.K.-based group, according to amNY. Elbit is an Israeli arms manufacturer. Pro-Palestinian protesters have previously targeted Capital One over lines of credit to the company.

City Council Speaker Julie Menin called the vandalism deeply disturbing and unacceptable, amNY reported. She said she had been in contact with the NYPD. She asked whether it could be an antisemitic hate crime. No injuries were reported.
No arrests have been made. Police have not released a description of a suspect. The investigation is ongoing, according to amNY.

woman-beaten-and-robbed-on-central-parks.title: Woman Beaten and Robbed on Central Park's East Drive; Three Suspects Sought
woman-beaten-and-robbed-on-central-parks.dek: Sunday night, near 90th Street. Three people struck a 32-year-old woman and fled with her backpack, police say.
body: Sunday evening. Central Park's East Drive near 90th Street. A 32-year-old woman was beaten and robbed while walking, Hoodline reported, citing police.

About 9:45 p.m., according to Hoodline. Police said three unidentified people struck the woman repeatedly in the head. They fled with her backpack. PIX11 reported the suspects were last seen heading toward Fifth Avenue.

EMS responded. The woman refused medical attention, Hoodline reported. Police have not released descriptions of the suspects. The park is open daily from 6 a.m. to 1 a.m. It is patrolled by the NYPD's Central Park Precinct.
Hoodline noted earlier incidents along East Drive. On Sept. 17, there were four gunpoint robberies within about an hour. Three men on bicycles took cellphones, according to West Side Rag.
No arrests have been made. The investigation is ongoing, according to Hoodline. Anyone with information can contact Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS.

williamsbridge-woman-27-has-phone-snatch.title: Williamsbridge Woman, 27, Has Phone Snatched From Pocket
williamsbridge-woman-27-has-phone-snatch.dek: August, near Capuchin Way and East Gun Hill Road. A man took a woman's cellphone from her back pocket. Police are seeking him.
body: Near Capuchin Way and East Gun Hill Road in Williamsbridge, the Bronx. A man took a 27-year-old woman's cellphone from her back pocket. Police are searching for him, Hoodline reported.
Aug. 25, according to police, as cited by Hoodline. The man walked up behind the woman. He grabbed the phone. He fled on foot, News 12 New York reported.
Police described the suspect as a man last seen wearing a black tank top and black pants, according to Hoodline. The location is on a busy stretch of East Gun Hill Road near the Bx30 bus line.

The 47th Precinct is investigating, Hoodline reported. NYPD CompStat data through Oct. 11 show 618 grand larceny complaints in the precinct this year. That is down 22.6% from 798 at the same point in 2025.

The suspect remains at large. No arrest has been reported. Hoodline did not explain why the August incident was being publicized in October. Anyone with information can call NYPD Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS.
